notes.before: Comparative molecular analysis for acquired toceranib resistance.
notes.after: Observational molecular/biomarker study of acquired toceranib resistance, including paired tumor/blood sampling. Currently enrolling, but excluded from treatment matching: standard Palladia, routine assessments and additional care remain owner-paid; $300 enrollment and possible $700 completion incentives support study-related veterinary services rather than a defined funded anticancer-treatment program.

funding.before: Current public listing does not expose complete owner-cost/funding terms; confirm during Anivive prescreen.
funding.after: 🟡 Partially funded. Laverdia-CA1 is provided free; sponsor contributes $150 per carboplatin visit (up to $600) and $25 per bloodwork visit (up to $100), with a 10% bill discount. Owners pay all additional costs and unrelated tests/procedures.

notes.before: Canine osteosarcoma. Current public marketplace confirms Recruiting but does not expose enough detailed patient-level eligibility/site data in the indexed listing; keep individual matches Possible until Anivive prescreen.
notes.after: Published official protocol lists one site, Cornell University Hospital for Animals. Dogs must already have undergone limb amputation for osteosarcoma at Cornell and must not have received any chemotherapy. Twelve-week study combines carboplatin with oral Laverdia-CA1 (verdinexor). Follow-up appointments and home medication administration are required. Current Anivive marketplace labels the study Recruiting; an older Cornell award page dates the original project to June 2022–May 2023, so current patient admission remains subject to Cornell prescreen.

why.before: Anivive's current Join Studies marketplace explicitly labels this osteosarcoma interventional study Recruiting.
why.after: Current official Anivive marketplace labels the exact Cornell SINE/verdinexor + carboplatin protocol Recruiting; individual protocol specifies Cornell, eligibility and partial cost support.

after.title: Autogenic tumor-RNA vaccine for Boxer dogs with suspected malignant glioma
after.status: Currently recruiting on the official neurology index and protocol heading
after.intervention: Autogenic vaccine prepared from RNA extracted from the patient's glioma biopsy; three weekly vaccinations beginning two weeks after biopsy
after.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. Study covers CT-guided tumor biopsy and lymph-node removal, associated anesthesia/recovery, study vaccines, and research sample collection/analysis. Other visit/care costs are not itemized and must be discussed at evaluation.
after.contact: Neurology Staff, University of Florida Small Animal Hospital: 352-392-2235; official Study Interest Form. PI: Dr. Sheila Carrera-Justiz.
after.eligibility: Boxer dogs with suspected malignant glioma on a previous MRI, no other life-threatening diseases and no previous treatment for the tumor. Neurology team confirms final eligibility.
after.notes: The current official UF neurology index explicitly lists NOW RECRUITING and the individual protocol heading repeats it, although one background sentence uses past-tense recruited. Prior MRI evidence of suspected malignant glioma is sufficient for prescreen; biopsy occurs in the study. Boxer breed restriction is mandatory and requires investigator confirmation because the current matcher does not encode breed. Tumor biopsy is followed by three weekly vaccines starting two weeks later. Lymph-node removal follows the first vaccination; each vaccine requires at least six hours in hospital for monitoring. No previous tumor treatment is permitted. This is a distinct UF glioma protocol, not the Minnesota Zika/autologous-lysate or nanoparticle-gene protocols.
